members.name: intraday_range_reversion_v1
members.thesis: When a stock touches its intraday high or low and immediately reverses on a specific bar pattern (pin bar / hammer at the extreme), it signals that the intraday range boundary has been defended. The intraday high/low acts as a natural support/resistance because algorithmic stop-placement and limit-o
entry_short: (high - close) / (high - low) > 0.7 (inverted pin bar / shooting star)
members.exit_target: 50% of intraday range toward the midpoint: (session_high + session_low) / 2
members.exit_stop: 0.15% beyond the session extreme (beyond session low for longs, beyond session high for shorts)
filters: India_VIX between 14-22; too low = no range, too high = range breaks easily
no entries before 10:00 (let range establish) or after 14:45
volume on pin bar > SMA(volume, 20) (volume at the extreme is essential)
prefer longs when price is above VWAP session midpoint (bullish bias)
weaknesses: On genuine breakout days, the first touch of the session extreme IS the breakout — strategy catches the wrong side
Pin bar recognition on 1-min bars is noisy; the pattern is more reliable on 5-min or 15-min bars
The 50% range reversion target is ambitious — many reversions stall at 20-30% of range

members.name: trend_counter_trend_v1
members.thesis: Trend-following strategies on 1-min bars capture large intraday moves but give back significant profit at reversals because trailing stops lag. filters: Widen stops to 1.5 * ATR(14) when India VIX > 22
No entries after 15:10 IST; no entries before 09:20
weaknesses: Lower win rate (45%) means longer losing streaks; need psychological discipline and sufficient capital to survive 8-10 consecutive losses
RSI divergence detection on 1-min bars is inherently noisy — false divergences are common and may trigger premature exits, cutting winners short
Supertrend(10, 3.0) on 1-min bars can whipsaw during the first hour when volatility is highest, generating false entries
members.prior_art: Supertrend indicator by Olivier Seban; RSI divergence widely used in technical analysis; asymmetric entry/exit discussed in Kaufman's 'Trading Systems and Methods'
